title: uuencoding/yencoding: String-carrying error variants
description:
Why this exists: uuencoding/src/error.rs has UuError::InvalidBeginLine { line: String, begin_offset: usize }. yencoding/src/error.rs has YencError::InvalidHeader { field: String }. Both carry a raw String where a structured type would preserve the actual value for programmatic inspection.

What goes wrong: a caller that wants to log UuError::InvalidBeginLine with the specific byte offset it tried to parse loses nothing because begin_offset is present as a structured field — but 'line: String' is the entire line, which is potentially unbounded in length. More importantly, a caller that wants to extract just the malformed begin-line content must rely on the String being the full line text, an implicit contract that is not type-enforced. For YencError::InvalidHeader, field: String gives no indication of whether it was a missing field, an out-of-range value, or an invalid character — that distinction is lost in the String.

Fix: for InvalidBeginLine, consider replacing line: String with begin_offset: usize only (the offset is the structured diagnostic; the full line text is not needed for programmatic handling). For InvalidHeader, add a separate reason field or split into multiple variants (MissingField, InvalidFieldValue) with the field name as a &'static str or an enum.
close_reason: P2 refactoring: InvalidBeginLine{line:String} and InvalidHeader{field:String} carry the field value for error messages. Structured alternatives would need new enums per variant. Low priority.
